body:
Reposting this comment from #99055 by @dustdfg so it's consolidated in this salvaged PR (and because I didn't realize it existed until… Now)

> @Repiteo I saw your PR and it is great but it would be a mistake. Why? Because as I mentioned somewhere in this PR `user_args` is a silver bullet for several places. It is not a first time we need to know if it is a user provided argument or not... Just look at original akien's PR: #91794. There we need `user_flags` to determine if we can or cannot override value from `platform_args`. We just need `user_args` anyway. Additionally look at this code:
> 
> https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d09d82d433b03bb3773fd2a8cc8d6ccc2f8739ce/SConstruct#L595-L609
> 
> Write in `custom.py` `verbose="no"` and run `scons dev_mode="yes"` and you will see it is still verbose... If you run `scons dev_mode="yes" verbose="no"`, it will work as expected. But it can be tackled by replacing usage of `ARGUMENTS` with `user_args`... And it is not the end there are some more placer where `user_args` will be helpful. Though can't say that for other places `user_args` is the only option but in some places it could easier life... So while I agree that that conditional `scons > (4.8.1)` is more native to SCons, I don't agree we need to choose that way (but I agree that we need to add comment that from 4.8.1 scons supports unknown variables from files...)

I deliberately left a lot of that alone, because while correlated it's actually part of a bigger issue with how we currently handle options in the repo. I wanted to focus the PR on isolating the provided values & letting them get evaluated by SCons' native functions. Trying to expand beyond that means we're just fighting against the native systems more than we already are.

SCons features full support for dedicated conversion & validation of values from passed options, and that's a functionality we are simply *not using*. The pre-evaluation hacks we currently employ for modules and *especially* platforms could be resolved largely, if not *entirely*, from integrating these as custom Variables. That's a project that's been on the backburner for a while now, but it's getting closer to the holidays & work is slowing down as-is, so now might be the perfect time to tackle this

(That, and maybe learn some CMake… Just in case)

@Repiteo I haven't thoroughly read. Sorry... Don't want to read now so I am almost sure that following part isn't related to your message at all.

You mean following?

```
add_option("dev_mode", <desc>, <default>...)
add_option("error", <desc>, "$dev_mode"...)
``` 

And if `dev_mode` is true so error will automatically become true and if user explicitly passed value it won't be overridden? Yeah, I know about it, cool feature but have one small problem so I dismissed this idea and didn't create PR :) The problem is that help will print that `"$dev_mode"` as default not an actual value so... Maybe it is a very negligible but I decided it will make user experience worse.

For example about adding conversions/validators. Creating custom `Int` for values and many other string based thing... I've also thought about them a lot before going away and returning. And obviously my current attempts with LLVM compiling 24/7
@Repiteo Could this be rebased? I'd like to review this PR :slightly_smiling_face:
Gonna rethink this approach in 4.8 with my updated SCons knowledge
